audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup's focus ability is a fabricated name: 'Subject: Fear (CC Paints)'. It appears in focus.text, winCon, enemyWin, loading, breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.feeding, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d and three report entries. No such ability exists.
audit.why: Hwei's E is Subject: Torment (12/11.5/11/10.5/10s), and Riot's text names its three paints: Grim Visage, Gaze of the Abyss, Crushing Maw. The page's underlying claim — that all his crowd control sits on one palette — is correct; only the name was invented.
audit.corrected: Every occurrence replaced with Subject: Torment, and the real sub-spell names plus the 12-second cooldown used where the advice needed to be concrete.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full layer said 'Skill' on all seven rows against the content/packet chart of Hwei/Hwei/Skill/Annie/Annie/Annie/Hwei.
audit.why: He out-ranges 625 with every paint at levels 1-2; Annie takes 4 through first item on stun-punish; he retakes the game at two items where palette depth plus Spiraling Despair outscales one combo.
audit.corrected: phases[].side aligned to the packet chart with ratings and whys following.

audit.whatIsWrong: The mid and late text call Spiraling Despair 'a long-range execute' that 'disabl[es] your engage options'.
audit.why: Riot text: the first champion struck becomes the centre of an expanding painting that slows and damages nearby enemies, exploding at max size or when that champion dies. It is a 1300-range slow-and-zone on 120/100/80s — not an execute and not a disable.
audit.corrected: Both passages rewritten around the sticking-target slow and the 1300 range.
sources: enemyKit R text, range and cooldown

audit.whatIsWrong: Signature of the Visionary was never mentioned, so nothing told you why eating one poke is survivable and eating two is not.
audit.why: Riot text: the first damaging spell primes, a second damaging spell completes the signature, which detonates after a short delay for area damage. That two-hit rule is the actual trading law of this lane.
audit.corrected: Written into phases[3].why and dosFull[1].d — leave after the first paint clips you.

edits.after: His poke loses value as your stun comes online: Subject: Disaster is 10s at rank 1, so trades taken inside that gap are a coin flip on execution.

edits.before: Hwei's ultimate adds a devastating extra burst/crowd-control layer to his kit, but it requires setup and vision that your Tibbers all-in can beat if you get there first.
edits.after: Spiraling Despair sticks to the first champion it hits from 1300 range and expands into a slow, but it needs vision, and your Tibbers all-in beats it if you arrive first.

edits.before: Fully scaled Hwei's combo of Q variants plus ultimate is one of the highest raw burst-and-CC packages in the game, edging back ahead of Annie's single-target kill threat.
edits.after: Fully scaled, Subject: Disaster into Subject: Torment plus Spiraling Despair is one of the highest burst-and-CC packages in the game, well ahead of Annie's one combo.

edits.before: From levels 4-6 you pull ahead: Hwei's combos require real setup time and his root/burst sequence can be punished hard if you engage the instant Pyromania is armed. Tibbers gives you a strong follow-up all-in tool at 6 that can close the distance his poke normally protects. Be careful once he hits 6 too — his ultimate adds a long-range execute and utility layer that can turn a losing fight around, so don't overextend even while ahead.
edits.after: From levels 4-6 you pull ahead: Hwei's paints need real setup time and his root-into-burst sequence is punishable if you engage the instant Pyromania is armed. Tibbers gives you a follow-up all-in at 6 that closes the distance his poke normally protects. Be careful once he hits 6 too — Spiraling Despair reaches 1300 and slows your entire approach, so don't overextend even while ahead.

edits.before: A fully itemized Hwei has one of the scariest burst-plus-CC toolkits in the game: his ultimate alone can shred through half a health bar while also disabling your engage options. Annie's stun-Tibbers combo is still lethal if you can close the gap unseen, but Hwei's range and combo depth mean he often dictates engagements from a position you can't easily punish. Flank through fog of war and pick your moments — a head-on approach in the late game favors him.
edits.after: A fully itemized Hwei has one of the scariest burst-plus-CC toolkits in the game: Spiraling Despair sticks to the first champion it hits and expands into a slow that stops your approach dead. Annie's stun-Tibbers is still lethal if you close the gap unseen, but his range and palette depth mean he dictates engagements from where you cannot punish him. Flank through fog and pick your moment — head-on, the late game favors him.

notes: Fabricated ability name found and removed everywhere it was writable: 'Subject: Fear (CC Paints)' does not exist — Hwei's E is Subject: Torment, whose paints are Grim Visage, Gaze of the Abyss and Crushing Maw. The page's claim that all his crowd control sits on one palette was correct, so only the name and the missing cooldown needed fixing. Second correction: Spiraling Despair was described as a 'long-range execute' that disables engage; it is a 1300-range sticking zone that slows and explodes at max size or on the anchor's death.
